AttachmentMaterializationReason.description: Why a request omitted an attachment.

oneOf.description: The target model and its route cannot accept this MIME/position pair.

generation_disposition.description:
Which of the caller's generation options this attempt's request
carried, as reported by the adapter that built it.

usage.description: Provider-reported usage only. Absence is not zero usage.

CancelOrigin.description:
The runtime or actor decision that requested cancellation of a process
or of a tool call's attempt. `RunClosing` is a call's owning tool Run
discharging its cancellation at Closing while the turn itself runs on.

CausalRef.description: Stable semantic reference to the runtime fact that caused another fact.

CellDefect.description: A rule of a session's cells that a cell's program broke.

oneOf.description:
The cell used a binding an earlier cell left that held a function or
a task: neither outlives the cell that created it, so the binding
was not carried.

The cell ended with tasks it started and did not await: some still
running, some failed with an error nothing observed. Each is named
by the site that started it and which run of that site it was.

CellFailure.description: Structured failure returned by a code executor.

defect.description:
The rule of a session's cells the program broke, when that is why
the cell failed, kept typed through the plugin and host result.

exec_failure.description:
Why the `exec_code` effect failed before the executor produced a
response, when that is the failure: the closed reason, kept typed
through the protocol driver and the trajectory it records.

feedback.description:
Each pure repair callback's identity and answer, in registration order,
including empty answers. Retained with the failure for replay and attribution.

tool_call_limit.description:
The session's `max_tool_calls` refusal, when that is why the cell
failed (FIG-4546), kept typed through the plugin and host result.

worker_limit.description: The measured run limit, kept typed through the plugin and host result.

CellFailureKind.description: Why an executed code cell failed.

oneOf.description: The runtime refused the program because it violates a dialect or policy bound.
The authored program failed to compile or execute correctly.
Host infrastructure failed while preparing or executing the program.

The worker does not hold the package set the cell is written under
(FIG-6918). The host can serve the work on a node that holds it.

CellFailureRepair.description: One plugin callback's recorded repair decision for a failed cell.

callback.description: The complete callback key, including its slot prefix.

ChargeSafetyDenialReason.description:
Why host charge-safety policy denied an otherwise transport-retryable
generation.

# Integrator class

Runtime and reporting implementors exhaustively render these host-policy
outcomes; provider adapters never construct them.

oneOf.description: Host policy requires a provider idempotency or resume guarantee.
The per-call unsafe retry allowance is exhausted.
Provider-reported tokens exceed the host's duplicate-cost bound.

ContentCategory.description:
Every content field belongs to one of these categories. Reasoning also
requires consent to its message's direction.

ContentMarks.description: How a reader distinguishes omitted, empty, cut and oversized content.

references.description: References committed by a normally returning content hook.

EffectAddress.description: Canonical address of one admitted runtime effect.

ExecCodeFailureReason.description:
Why an `exec_code` effect failed before the executor produced a response.

This is the closed classification offline trace analysis keys on; the human
detail lives in [`ExecCodeFailure::message`]. Serialized snake_case on the
durable journal and trace surfaces.

oneOf.description: No code executor is installed on the session.
The executor's language runtime exited unexpectedly.
Any other session-layer failure; `message` carries the detail.

ExecutionEvidence.description:
Facts reported by the provider about the execution that produced a response.

These fields must never be filled from request intent. In particular,
`reasoning_output_tokens: Some(0)` is distinct from an unreported value.

collection_interruption.description:
Why provider evidence is partial even though the Lash response is
accepted. Present only when Lash deliberately preempted collection.

provider_finish_reason.description:
Provider-reported terminal reason in that provider's own vocabulary.
Compatible gateways prefer their native reason over a normalized
OpenAI-compatible `finish_reason` when both are present.

provider_request_id.description:
Transport request identifier reported by the provider (for example,
OpenRouter's `x-request-id`). This is distinct from the response's
protocol-level identifier and may be present on failed attempts.

ExecutionScope.description:
Stable semantic identity for one effectful runtime operation.

This is the scope admitted by the host boundary before nondeterministic
work begins. Its journal encoding is an existing durable contract; effect
addresses compose it with a replay key without changing those bytes.

oneOf.description:
One operation on a session that runs no turn: a host command, named
by its batch, or the admissions of one shift request. It has no
logical root, and no logical turn runs under it.

ExtensionAttribute.description: One contributed attribute, as the bounded writer admitted it.

ExtensionContent.description: One content value an extension built under the `extension` category.

ExtensionOperation.description:
The GenAI operation a typed [`SpanSpec`] preset declares. Lash sets its
semconv attributes; a plugin cannot set them through `attr`.

oneOf.description: `embeddings {gen_ai.request.model}`.
`retrieval {gen_ai.data_source.id}`.
The plugin called `end`.
The handle was dropped.
The body returned with the span still open.
The body future was dropped with the span still open.
The body unwound with the span still open.

The body's publication hold was full: lash finalized the span early so
the records held under it could publish.

ExtensionSpanEvent.description: One event an extension recorded on its span.

ExtensionSpanKind.description: The OpenTelemetry kind of an extension span.

ExtensionSpanRecord.description:
The one record of an extension span (or point): emitted when it ends,
whole, with everything it buffered.

`plugin_id` and `callback` are the registered callback the span's
capability was bound from, never a value the plugin supplied.

contents.description:
Serialized as `contents`: the record envelope's `content` is its
content marks, and the record flattens this one beside them.

error_type.description: Set when the plugin called `fail`: the span's `error.type`.

point.description: A zero-duration point recorded with no open span.

GenerationOptionOutcome.description:
What became of one host-set generation setting on one request.

A setting a host sets is sent, or the call is refused before any I/O with a
typed failure; nothing is silently dropped. The receipt therefore names only
the two deliberate non-send dispositions besides `Applied`: a cap reduced to
the model's capacity, and stop sequences a protocol owns. `Applied` means
lash put the value on the wire, never that the provider complied.

oneOf.description: The host expressed no preference, so there was nothing to apply.
The host asked for it and the request carries it.

A protocol suppressed the caller's non-empty stop list because its
grammar owns the response boundary. This is intentional protocol
ownership, but the caller's requested value did not reach the wire.

Explicit prompt-cache breakpoints the protocol placed that this
adapter's wire has no cache directive for. Only the `cache` row, which
reports protocol-placed breakpoints rather than a host setting, uses it.

The caller asked for an output-token cap above what this model can
produce, and the request carries the model's capacity instead. The
bound the caller asked for still holds; the number on the wire is
smaller than the one they named.

output_token_cap.description:
Upper bound on output tokens. Unset means lash sends no cap on wires
where one is optional; a wire that requires one takes the provider
options' `max_output_tokens` or refuses the call.

parallel_tool_calls.description:
Whether the model may call several tools in one response. Unset sends
nothing; a wire with no such control refuses a set value.

seed.description:
Sampling seed, a best-effort repeatability request. Carried by the
OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions dialect and Google's
`generationConfig`; every other wire refuses a set seed.

stop_sequences.description:
Literal sequences that terminate generation. Wires without a native
stop-sequence field refuse a non-empty list. A protocol whose grammar
owns the response boundary may suppress this entire list; the resulting
disposition is `SuppressedProtocolOwned`, not `Applied`.

temperature.description:
Sampling temperature. A wire that has no temperature field, or a model
that pins sampling, refuses a set temperature before any I/O; `None`
leaves the endpoint default in place.

GenerationReceipt.description:
Per-call account of every host generation setting: resolution supplies
what was requested, the adapter supplies what it emitted.

This is request-side, adapter-owned bookkeeping and deliberately separate
from [`ExecutionEvidence`], which carries only facts the provider reported
about the execution.

cache.description: Fate of explicit prompt-cache breakpoints in the request.

output_token_cap.description: The effective cap: the request's, else the provider options'.

reasoning.description: The model spec's reasoning selection; `ProviderDefault` is not a request.

reasoning_retention.description: The model spec's reasoning-history retention selection.

thinking_summary.description:
`expose_thinking`'s wire half: a reasoning summary requested from the
provider.

thinking_visibility.description: `expose_thinking`'s local half: reasoning output published to the host.

oneOf.description:
Model "thinking" / reasoning output from providers that expose a
chain-of-thought channel.

* `text` — human-readable summary for display.
* `replay` — opaque provider replay state. Provider crates decide
  how to map it back to their wire format on the next turn.

replay.description:
Opaque provider replay state. Core may use `item_id` for stable
correlation, but provider crates own the wire semantics.

LlmProviderTraceDirection.description:
Which way a raw provider observation travelled, with the name its side
of the wire gives it.

oneOf.description: The serialized request Lash sent to `endpoint`.

One event of the provider's response. `event_name` is the vendor's
own spelling, kept as raw evidence and never interpreted.

unknown_calls.description:
Model calls whose provider usage never reached lash, so none of their
tokens are in the counters above (ADR 0031): a sum with a nonzero count
is a lower bound, never a total. A single call's usage counts itself.

MaxToolCalls.description:
The number of tool calls one execution may make: the host's required
decision, with no default and no built-in ceiling (FIG-4546).

What it counts depends on the execution. A cell — one code cell of a turn,
or one tool step of a protocol without cells — may make at most this many
tool calls in total. A process may hold at most this many at once: a call
counts from its acceptance until the process no longer depends on it, so
a long-running process is bounded in what it retains, never in what it
does over its life. The call that passes the limit fails with
[`ToolCallLimitExceeded`]; every call under it runs untouched. The limit
paces nothing: rate limits and throttling are the host's own.

Name.description:
A variable, parameter or declared-function name.

Any text is a name; the kernel gives none of them meaning. Structural
validation refuses the empty name.

NormalizedError.description: A journal-safe projection of a provider/transport failure.

code.description:
The failure code, namespaced by who authored the spelling: `lash:` for
workspace-authored codes, `provider:` for provider wire vocabulary,
and a host's own namespace for host-authored codes.

ProcessStartPhase.description:
A phase of a host process start, in the order a start passes them. Each
phase a start reached carries its duration on the start's producer.

oneOf.description:
The host call before staging: the start key, the session-turn check
and the effect's dispatch.

The recorded admission: the host session's liveness and the
session-turn admission.

Staging the execution environment under the start's claim and
reading it back.
Reading and decoding the stored definition descriptor.

The engine deriving the definition's signature, including reading
its document and any cache lookup or decode that read needs.

Acquiring the definition's artifact closure under the start's
claim, including store transactions and their lock waits.

Verifying the host's signature claim against the stored definition,
including the engine's independent derivation.

Building the definition's start payload, or realizing a function
the start carries inline. The named definition operations above
have their own disjoint timings.
The engine's admission of the payload and of its sealed settings.
Holding the engine artifacts the payload names.

The link check: the effects the payload performs against the
environment's links and this node's components.
Staging the input's attachments.
Preparing the registration.
The registrar's transaction.
Holding what the registered row adopts under its record.
Reading the registered process back for the receipt.

ProcessStartPhaseTime.description: How long a process start spent in one phase, in microseconds.

ProducerKind.description: The host call a producer span stands for.

oneOf.description: A send of one input.
A batch send.
A host process start.
A host tool-intent submission.
A plugin operation invoked through the host admin surface.
The observing process was lost; no observations survived.

ProviderFailureKind.description:
Classification of a provider/transport failure.

This is the single canonical failure-kind vocabulary: provider transports
classify failures into it (`lash-core` re-exports it from
`llm::transport`), the turn machine carries it on
[`ErrorEnvelope`](crate::session_model::ErrorEnvelope), and hosts read it
back from `TurnIssue`s without scraping traces.

`Unknown` is an explicit classification, never a decoder fallback.
Persisted failure records reject unrecognized kind literals.

origin.description:
Exact LLM Provider route that minted this reasoning replay state.
Missing on sessions persisted before replay provenance was introduced.

Exact LLM Provider route that minted this opaque replay state. Missing
on sessions persisted before replay provenance was introduced.

ProviderRouteIdentity.description:
Stable identity of one configured LLM Provider route.

`endpoint` is either a normalized base URL or a host-supplied opaque route
id. Together with the LLM Provider kind and requested model it is the replay
contract. Model aliases behind one endpoint are intentionally out of scope:
hosts must use the exact model string they want included in route equality.
HTTP(S) endpoints reject userinfo because credentials are neither route
identity nor safe trace metadata. Explicit default ports remain distinct
from implicit ports. Scheme and host case, plus an empty path versus `/`,
normalize; path case and query strings remain identity-significant.

ResponsePhase.description:
Provider replay phase tag: the two-value vocabulary the kernel interprets
(`"commentary"`/`"final_answer"` on the wire). An unknown spelling fails
decoding rather than silently meaning "neither".

origin.description:
Exact LLM Provider route that minted this provider-owned response
metadata. Missing on sessions persisted before replay provenance was
introduced.

provider_payload.description:
Provider-owned payload needed to replay this text part on a future
request. The kernel stores it opaquely and providers decide whether it
is valid for their next wire request.

RetryClass.description: Evidence that permits another provider attempt.

RetryDecision.description: The sealed decision for a prospective provider retry.

oneOf.description: The call's limit expired: the model total ends every further attempt.

RunAggregateWakePolicy.description:
Aggregate wake rule. Run-owned aggregates preserve these semantics;
the rule does not require a durable group dispatcher.

`Promise.all` and `Promise.allSettled` both use [`All`](Self::All): the
caller's early exit on rejection is not a host wake rule. The wire shape
has no default, so a missing rule cannot be replayed under a guess.

oneOf.description: Wake on the first settlement of any kind.
Wake on the first success, or after every child fails.
Deliver every settlement in durable rank order.

RunObservation.description: Per-run observation. Off is unobserved, never a zero count.

RuntimeOwner.description:
Who a runtime runs for: a session, or a process named by its minted id.

A session runtime and a process runtime cross the same interfaces — the
plugin session, the tool catalog, the attachment facade, the authority a
tool intent is declared under — and those interfaces take a
`RuntimeOwner`. A process runtime is never handed a session id as a
stand-in for its own identity.

oneOf.description:
A composition whose members no kernel type states, or whose meet
grows past the projection's bound
([`lash_kernel_check::MAX_PROJECTED_TYPE_NODES`]), at the JSON
pointer `schema_path`: a value of the schema could not be typed.

Site.description:
A node's address: the code it belongs to and the chain of
[`Node::children`] indexes that reaches it from that code's body.

A site is derived from the document and is never written by a host
(`K-ID-004`). An empty chain addresses the body itself.

SpanRole.description: What a record is to the span it names.

oneOf.description:
A live hint that the span started. Its span may never close if its
execution dies first.

The span's one closing record, published under the closure rules: it
carries the span's exported start and end.
A span opened and closed by this one record.
A live record inside the span.

StepBodyStarted.description:
The admitted body of a process step started: the step's actor committed
its admission, bound it to a call, and is about to run it. A step that is
refused never produces one, and a retried body produces one more with the
same site, occurrence and call and the next attempt.

It names no language and no document: the process's own definition scopes
the site.

at.description:
The occurrence of the site in the process's workflow document the
step runs for.

attempt.description: The one-based attempt of the admitted body.

call_id.description: The call the admission bound the step to.

StreamBlockEvent.description:
One step of a streamed output block's lifecycle: the single payload every
lane carries for it — the provider stream, the session stream, turn
activity and the trace. A lane adds its own envelope (observation
identity, correlation, sequence, elapsed time) around this payload and
never redefines it.

oneOf.description: The next suffix of `block`'s text.

`block` closed. `text` is the block's authoritative text, so a
consumer can correct drift from accumulated deltas.

StreamBlockIdentity.description:
Provider-minted identity of one streamed output block.

Minted by the provider adapter from provider facts: OpenAI
`(item_id, summary_index)`, Anthropic content-block index, or a
deterministic per-attempt ordinal for providers with no native notion.
The id is opaque to hosts; ordering comes from `ordinal`, never from
parsing `id`. Live and replayed streams emit identical identities.

id.description: Opaque provider-minted block key, stable within one response attempt.

item_id.description:
The reasoning or message item this block belongs to, when the provider
has one. N blocks may share one item's replay material.

ordinal.description: Per-attempt block ordinal assigned by the provider adapter.

StreamBlockKind.description:
Which render lane a streamed output block belongs to.

A *block* is the unit a host renders: one OpenAI reasoning summary part,
one Anthropic `thinking`/`text` content block, or one ordinal run of
thought/text for providers with no native notion. Blocks name their owning
reasoning item or message item when the provider has one; several blocks
may share one item's replay material.

oneOf.description: Visible assistant prose.

Reasoning summary ("thinking") text, kept separate from assistant
response text.

ToolCallLimitExceeded.description:
A tool call refused by the session's [`MaxToolCalls`]: the program asked
for more tool calls than its recorded limit admits.

It is the program's failure, never the host's: the limit is recorded
config and the count is a fact of the program's own history, so a replay
or a redrive refuses the same call. Nothing of the refused calls is
journaled or dispatched.

counted.description:
The calls counted against the limit before the refused ones: made so
far by a cell, held now by a process.

limit.description: The recorded `max_tool_calls` the execution runs under.

requested.description:
The calls refused together: one for a single call, an aggregate's
unique tool calls for an aggregate.

oneOf.description: A cell: the limit is the total it may make.
A process: the limit is what it may hold at once.

ToolCheckConflict.description:
The terminal reply a tool check's reduction selected and every terminal
reply it displaced, in reduction order.

ToolCheckPhase.description: The built-in tool check phase a reply was given in.

ToolCheckReply.description: One callback's reply to a tool check, attributed to its plugin.

ToolCheckVerdictKind.description: What a tool check callback decided, without the decision's payload.

execution_scope_id.description:
The enclosing execution-scope id: a turn id for turn scope and a
process id for process scope.

minting_emission_replay_key.description:
Replay key of the durable invocation that minted this declaration,
retained so `replay_key` stays re-derivable from the record alone.
`None` for host-submitted intents, whose identity binds no emission.

owner.description:
The runtime whose authority declared the intent: a session, or a
process runtime.

ToolIntentKind.description:
Literal command kind of one recorded declaration.

Generated from [`tool_intent_variants!`]; never hand-edited.

ToolSpanAnnotations.description:
The attributes a tool body set on its own `execute_tool` span, through
its bounded writer. Held in memory with the attempt that set them and
stamped by the span's closer; never persisted.

delivery_form.description: The delivery form name. Absent on a logical summary taken before send.

TraceAttemptLink.description:
The durable-substrate attempt a handler is executing under, as that
substrate's transport delivered it.

It is an optional capability of the substrate seam: a substrate with no
attempt notion reports none. A record it makes carries it in its
position, and its span links the attempt's context; it never becomes an
operation's parent and is never stored.

context.description:
The attempt span the substrate injected, absent when its tracing is
off or the header was malformed.

invocation_id.description: The substrate's invocation id, when the delivery names one.

TraceAttemptObservation.description:
What the provider seam observed around one dispatched attempt. The
attempt's facts are its sealed `AttemptRecord`, reported beside this.

ended_at_ms.description:
Wall-clock epoch milliseconds the attempt was sealed, when the
provider seam timed it.

provider.description: The provider that served the attempt, when the provider seam named it.

started_at_ms.description:
Wall-clock epoch milliseconds the attempt was dispatched, when the
provider seam timed it.

TraceContext.description:
A record's correlation: the stable ids it belongs to and the effect that
made it.

caused_by.description: The fact that caused the effect invocation that made the record.

graph_node_id.description:
The workflow-graph join key of a language-execution record: the
observed node's structural id, equal to the `WorkflowGraph` node id
(ADR 0100 R0). A child start carries its parent node's id, and
execution start and finish leave it unset.

replay_key.description: The replay key of the effect invocation that made the record.

send_id.description: The turn's head input, or a producer's accepted input.

TraceCountObservation.description:
A count observation owns the subject and coordinates that determine how
its counts accumulate. No optional field selects the arithmetic.

oneOf.description: Provisional deltas; committed `process.ran` remains authoritative.
Cumulative activation totals, folded by elementwise maximum.

TraceDomainCompletion.description: The terminal of one durable domain operation.

error_code.description: The typed failure code of a failed operation.

started_at_ms.description:
Wall-clock epoch milliseconds the operation's scope retained as its
start.

TraceDomainStatus.description: How a durable domain operation ended.

TraceDomainSubject.description: The durable domain operation a [`TraceEvent::DomainCompleted`] ends.

oneOf.description: One occurrence of a workflow node, by its whole effect identity.

TraceEffectEnvelopeDiffEvent.description:
Structural differences between the canonical envelopes on a failed durable
replay validation. This event may contain prompt and tool-result values and
must therefore only be emitted through the extended-trace gate.

TraceEffectEnvelopeDiffValue.description:
One side of a divergent canonical-envelope value.

Large values are omitted whole. Their exact serialized length and digest
remain available, but no prefix is retained.

oneOf.description:
The execution began. Its identity names the workflow document and
entry; the document itself is read through facade workflow inspection.
One fact about one occurrence of one execution site.
Statement starts and empty-block entries, with their accumulation law.

TraceLanguageExecutionFailure.description: The observed cause of a failed language node.

oneOf.description:
A dispatched tool effect failed with its recorded classification and
recorded source and delay hint. `replay_key` is the causing effect's identity.
A VM or host-boundary failure with a stable runtime error code.

omitted.description: Contexts dropped past the retained limit.

generation_disposition.description:
Which of the caller's generation options the adapter put on the wire.
Absent when the adapter does not report, which is not the same as
reporting that nothing was requested.

request_model.description: The model identifier requested for the corresponding LLM call.

TraceModelAttempt.description:
The execution attempt's facts, with trace metadata only for an attempt
that reached provider dispatch. A synthetic cut between attempts has no span.

generation_disposition.description:
Which of the caller's generation options this attempt's request
carried, as reported by the adapter that built it.

usage.description: Provider-reported usage only. Absence is not zero usage.

TraceModelAttemptSpan.description:
One real provider attempt's trace identity and provider-seam clocks.
Execution-local: none of these facts enters the stored execution ledger.

response_metadata_keys.description:
The keys of the response metadata the provider leaf captured for
this attempt (e.g. `header:x-opper-cost`), never their values.

terminal_delivery_timed_out.description: Lash stopped awaiting the host's terminal callback before it returned.

TraceModelCall.description:
Operational request facts retained until a logical model call closes.
These contain no captured prompt, tool schema or host telemetry label.

TraceNodeFact.description:
What happened to the occurrence a
[`TraceLanguageExecutionPayload::Node`] names.

oneOf.description:
Display attribution from an effect request. This does not start an
occurrence or change its identity, admission, counts or outcome.

The occurrence has parked on an observed wait. Its `since` is the
enclosing trace record timestamp, not a separately sampled clock.

A parked occurrence resolved, including cancellation. Its node
terminal remains a separate fact.
Only an occurrence observed in flight may be cancelled.

selected.description: The arm of the branch this occurrence took.

oneOf.description: The occurrence started a child execution.

TraceOmissionCounts.description: Omissions by reason: the non-zero reasons and their counts.

TraceOmissionDiagnostic.description:
One body's or one record's omissions with the address they happened at.
Bounded whatever the body did: one site and one fixed counter array.

TraceOmissionSite.description:
Where an omission happened: a stable lash address, never a host value.
Two bodies or two records never share one.

oneOf.description:
An extension body or a tool body's annotations: the registered
callback it was bound from, the span its capability was bound at,
and the admitted attempt it ran for.
One record's content-hook references or selector failure.
One exported span's enrichment, or a producer's sampler attributes.
Observations a shift held behind its journal frontier.
Links over the limit at a scope's admission or close.
Records an unanchored cell shed under hold pressure.

TracePosition.description:
A record's position: the span it opens, closes, is, or is an event of,
with that span's parent, links and real start.

The span's flags are its trace's sampling decision. `parent` is `None`
only for a producer with no caller.

attempt.description:
The substrate attempt that made the record, when the substrate
reports one: a link, never a parent.

ended_at.description: Set on a closing or whole record: the span's exported end.

scope.description: The span's logical owner, when a durable scope owns it.

started_at.description:
The span's real start; on a closing or whole record, its exported
start.

TraceProviderBodyOmission.description:
Why a provider observation's parsed `raw_json` view is absent although the
raw bytes were observed.

oneOf.description: The host's [`ContentPolicy`] policy withheld it.

TraceProviderEvent.description:
One raw provider observation of a model call: the request Lash sent or
one event of the provider's response.

raw_sha256.description:
SHA-256 of the exact wire bytes. `raw_json` is a parsed structured
view whose re-serialization may not reproduce these bytes.

TraceProviderReplayKind.description:
Opaque replay state rejected before an LLM Provider request was serialized.
A missing minting route identifies a session written before provenance was
introduced (or another unstamped producer); it is intentionally not
inferred from the currently selected route.

TraceRetryAttempt.description:
One tool attempt projected from its retry owner's sealed record. A model
call's attempts are its sealed `AttemptRecord`s, carried as they are.

TraceRuntimeStreamEvent.description: One decoded provider stream event, in the order the runtime folded it.

oneOf.description:
One step of a streamed block's lifecycle, as hosts saw it: the same
payload the session stream and turn activity carry, with the block's
full identity. Several blocks can share one item (OpenAI summary parts
of one reasoning item); the block's `ordinal` orders them.

raw_text.description:
The provider's text before stream transforms rewrote it, when it
was observed apart from the event's own text.

oneOf.description: A completed assistant-text part of the response.
A completed reasoning item of the response.
A completed tool call of the response.
Usage the provider reported mid-stream.

TraceScopeId.description:
A trace scope's identity: its owner and the owner's boundary ordinal.

Boundary 0 is the owner's admission. A later boundary of the same owner
(a process segment, a checkpoint that consumed new input) takes the next
ordinal the owner's own records already count. The id is separate from
every business identity preimage.

TraceScopeOwner.description:
The durable owner of a trace scope: the admitted thing whose work the
scope parents.

oneOf.description: One physical agent turn, including a follow-on within a run.
One tool call under its original logical owner.

One host-submitted tool intent, by its replay key, under the
runtime whose authority declared it: a session or a process.
A registered process, across all of its segments.

TraceSpanKind.description: The kind of span a record names: one row of the span taxonomy.

oneOf.description:
A host call that admits durable work: a trace's root or the caller's
child.
A turn.
One logical model call.
One real provider attempt of a model call.
One tool call.
One code cell.
A process that is not a user-facing workflow.
A workflow process.
One occurrence of a workflow node.
A host-submitted tool intent.
A span an extension opened.
A zero-duration point an extension recorded.

TraceToolArgs.description: Tool arguments observed at completion, distinct from arguments that are unavailable.

oneOf.description: The call's result: `ToolResults` content, `null` when omitted.

The call never settled: the session closed while it ran, and its
turn's terminal owner closed its span. It has no output.

TraceToolCancellation.description:
A cancelled call as a trace carries it: where the cancellation came from
and whether lash forced it, which survive every content policy, hook and
bound, and its governed [diagnostics](TraceToolCancellation::diagnostics).

diagnostics.description:
`ToolResults` content: one JSON object holding the cancellation's
`message`, and its `raw` evidence when it has it. Governed as
[`TraceToolFailure::diagnostics`] is.

TraceToolFailure.description:
A failed call as a trace carries it: the failure's classification, which
is structure and survives every content policy, hook and bound, and its
governed [diagnostics](TraceToolFailure::diagnostics).

diagnostics.description:
`ToolResults` content: one JSON object holding the failure's
`message`, and its `cause` and `raw` evidence when it has them. A
content hook sees it at the `tool_results` path, and may rewrite it
to any JSON value. Absent when that content is not captured, or was
omitted, offloaded or over its bound.

TraceToolName.description:
A tool's recorded name, or its identity when no recorded name is available.
Exporters use an identity to name the span, but omit `gen_ai.tool.name`.

TraceToolOwner.description: The logical owner of a tool call, independent of its execution route.

oneOf.description: The admitted logical run, whose turn id stays fixed across follow-ons.

TraceToolResultBlock.description:
One ordered block of a traced tool result: text, or an attachment at the
position the tool's value placed it.

TraceTurnCancellationEvidence.description:
Durable evidence that the traced turn was cancelled. Mirrors the runtime's
`TurnCancellationEvidence`, which only [`TurnStop::Cancelled`] can carry, so
a cancelled trace outcome can never be stated without saying which request
produced it.

[`TurnStop::Cancelled`]: lash_sansio::session_model::TurnStop::Cancelled

origin.description: Opaque host-domain data. Lash records and returns it unchanged.

oneOf.description: A declared Finish control ended the turn.

TraceTurnFailureReason.description:
Why a [`TraceTurnOutcome::Failed`] turn stopped. Mirrors the non-cancelled
`TurnStop` reasons.

oneOf.description: The durable follow-on reached its chain's frame-switch bound.

TraceTurnOutcome.description:
The single terminal outcome of a traced turn.

One closed shape replaces the former `status` / `done_reason` /
`agent_frame_switch` triple: each variant owns exactly the data its state
can carry, so an agent-frame switch cannot be reported without a frame key
and a cancellation cannot be reported without its evidence. Cancellation is
its own variant rather than a failure reason — [`Self::is_failed`] is
`false` for it.

oneOf.description: The turn reached a terminal result the caller asked for.
The turn ended by handing control to another agent frame.
The turn was cancelled. Not a failure.
The turn stopped short of a result.

TraceValue.description:
A contributed value. `Json` is the declared JSON exception of the
tracing seam.

Unit.description: The code a node belongs to.

oneOf.description: The document's `main`.
A declared function of the document.
The kernel-code body of a library function.

W3cSpanId.description: A nonzero W3C span id: 16 lowercase hex digits.

WorkerFrameKind.description: The worker message an encoder refused, without its guest data.

WorkerLimit.description: The VM or worker limit a run exhausted.

oneOf.description:
A step's execution observations outgrew the run's heap budget, which
bounds the stream a worker holds and hands its parent, or a single
observation outgrew what one frame carries (FIG-4458).
The encoded effect request or result exceeds its configured bound.
A parked run exceeds its configured bound.
A worker message cannot fit in one transport frame.

The execution's CPU time passed its configured budget: the parent's
cumulative accounting across the execution's attempts, or the CPU
ceiling the worker set from that budget (`SIGXCPU`).

One exchange computed or serialized past its configured wall-clock
deadline.

The worker's resident memory passed the `memory.max` of the cgroup
its host placed it in, and the kernel killed it (FIG-6787).

The execution held its workers past its configured wall time: the
sum over its checkouts, and for a code-mode cell over its
activations, of the time from a worker's admission to its release
(FIG-6786).
The execution spent its configured replacement attempts.

The host took longer than its configured host-read deadline to
answer one read (a clock, random, projection or planned-read answer,
or a limiter's decision) while the run held its worker. A durable
park releases its worker and has no such bound.
The document's `main`: a session cell.

One entry of the document: a declared function a host may start,
which is what a process runs.

WorkflowDocumentRef.description:
Which workflow document an execution runs, and where it enters it. It
names the document; it is never the document. A host reads the document
the reference names through the facade's workflow inspection and may
cache it under this value, which is immutable for a process: a running
instance keeps the document it was admitted under.

document.description:
The identity of the admitted kernel document: the hash of its
content, kernel version and manifest included.

entry.description: Where the execution enters the document.

description:
One durable trace record: the envelope fields plus the flattened
event, whose `type` tag names the variant.

oneOf.description:
A model call's prompt did not compose, so nothing was sent: the
decision evidence. `plan` is the resolved plan the composition ran
(absent when the plan itself did not resolve), `limits` the plan's
configured limits, `error` the typed failure with its site and the
measured bytes, and `elapsed_ms` the time the composition took.
One attachment was omitted so an otherwise valid session can continue.

attachment_position.description:
On the wire `attachment_position`: a record's own `position`
is its place in the trace.

oneOf.description:
Complete model-facing composition captured only when its fingerprint
changes for a resident session.

fingerprint.description:
SHA-256 of the rendered system prompt plus ordered fingerprints of
the model-facing tool contracts.

tool_schemas.description:
Full model-facing tool contracts in request order. This is kept
even when empty so the event is a self-contained snapshot.

oneOf.description:
One real provider request attempt of a model call, reported by the
body that dispatched it when the attempt is sealed. `attempt` is the
record the call's `attempts` ledger carries under the same ordinal. A
call that retried reports one per attempt.

The terminal of a durable domain operation that has no record of its
own kind: a process or a tool intent. It is a logical record of the
operation's scope.

provider_call_id.description: The model provider's id for the call, when a model issued it.

args.description: Exporters outside lash cannot read the store, so this diagnostic content travels with the trace.

attempts.description: Exporters outside lash cannot read the journal, so the observed retry ladder travels with the trace.

issuing_node_id.description: Exporters outside lash cannot read the store, so issuer correlation travels with the trace.

name.description: Exporters outside lash cannot read the store, so this diagnostic content travels with the trace.

output.description: Exporters outside lash cannot read the store, so this diagnostic content travels with the trace.

provider_call_id.description:
The model provider's id for the call, when a model issued it.
Exporters outside lash cannot read the store, so provider correlation travels with the trace.

span_attributes.description:
What the body of the attempt that settled the call set on its own
tool span: in memory only, stamped by the span's closer.

oneOf.description:
A code cell's span opens: once per execution of the cell, starting at
the cell's retained first start.

A code cell answered, and the commit that consumed its answer closes
its span. `started_at_ms` is the cell's first start, which a
suspension or a re-run keeps; `duration_ms` runs from it.

trailing_discarded.description: Observed bytes discarded after the model reply's first cell.

oneOf.description:
A code cell answered with a failure, and the commit that consumed its
answer closes its span, from its first start.

duration_ms.description: The observed window, absent when no invocation existed.

error.description: Human-readable detail. Not a stable classification surface.

reason.description:
Closed failure classification; offline analysis keys on this rather
than matching `error` prose.

trailing_discarded.description: Observed bytes discarded after the model reply's first cell.

oneOf.description:
A code cell its turn's terminal stopped before it answered: that
terminal's owner closes its span, from its first start. A discard is
not a failure.

trailing_discarded.description: Observed bytes discarded after the model reply's first cell.

oneOf.description: The runtime received a typed, non-retryable store integrity failure.

Compile/link evidence a protocol plugin reports before it executes a
program the model submitted as one protocol step.
The program compiled and linked successfully.
Setup, parsing, or linking rejected the program before execution.

diagnostic.description: Bounded compiler or linker feedback, using the raw-error trace limit.

step_index.description: Protocol iteration of the submitted program within its turn.

language.description:
The source dialect, when the execution records one. Graph artifacts
are dialect-free and leave it absent.

oneOf.description: The admitted body of a process step started.

inference_calls.description:
Model calls admitted by this turn, including failed calls; absent
when the terminal owner cannot recover that fact.

input.description: Admitted input messages, captured by the terminal owner from durable input.

output.description: The assistant answer this turn settled with, governed as OutputMessages.

oneOf.description:
A host call that admits durable work ended: its producer span's one
record.
This call's acceptance retained the cause.
A retry read back an earlier acceptance's cause.
The call failed before acceptance.
The host future was dropped or panicked before it settled.

phases.description: A process start's time per phase it reached, in phase order.

oneOf.description:
A built-in tool check selected one terminal reply over others. The
same fact reaches session observers as a plugin runtime event.

An extension span or point ended: its one whole record, with what
it buffered. Its position names the span and its parent.

What one extension body's contributions lost, with the body's
address: emitted once when the body exits, only when not empty.

A context-pressure hook's decision opened a compaction frame for the
turn. `task` is the frame's model-facing task.
